finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unvalidated `sort` GET parameter is concatenated into the query. Prepared statements cannot parameterize ORDER BY, and no allowlist is applied in this function. An attacker can run boolean or blind injection, for example `sort=(CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM users)='a' THEN id ELSE name END)`, to extract data from any table in the SQLite DB.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at line 6

trace.note: $sort is concatenated into the SQL string and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist or escaping on this path. list_users_safe (line 9-13) shows the allowlist mapping, but list_users_sorted does not use it. find_user (line 15-19) uses a bound parameter and is safe. No authentication or authorization check exists in the file.

verdict.guard_found: none in list_users_sorted; the allowlist in list_users_safe (list.php:10-11) is a separate function that is not used on this path
verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 does concatenate raw $_GET['sort'] into PDO::query with no allowlist, but list_users_sorted has no caller in the directory (grep finds only its definition), so I cannot confirm an attacker can reach it.
